 SCCH 15 3 MVC No.333/2021  :JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ for the death of L.C. Mahesh S/o L.B. Chikka Anjinappa in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 29.09.2020 at about 7.00 p.m., when the deceased L.C. Mahesh was crossing the road on Lakkondahalli - Shankanipura road, near Shubodaya hotel, Hoskote Taluk, at that time, one Chevrolet Beat LT bearing Reg.No.25Z1847 was driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed to the Mahesh and caused the accident.
Due to which, Mahesh had sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, deceased L.C. Mahesh was shifted to MVJ hospital.
But, the doctors had declared him as SCCH 15 4 MVC No.333/2021 dead.

Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as a Technician in Celebrations Apparel Limited and also doing Agriculture and Real estate and was earning a sum of Rs.3,00,000/ per month.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer and the Respondent No.3 is the driver of the offending Chevrolet Beat LT bearing Reg.No.25Z 1847.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

sentences.text: In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.3 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through its respective Counsels.
The Respondent No.1 did not choose to file Objection Statement.

The Respondent No.2 filed its detailed Objection Statement interalia denied the age, avocation and SCCH 15 5 MVC No.333/2021 income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also injuries sustained by the deceased in the said accident.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, my learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Mahesh sustained injuries due to rash and negligent act of driving of Chevrolet Beat LT bearing Reg.No.25Z1847 on dated 29.09.2020 at about 7.00 p.m., and succumbed to the injuries?
2) Whether the Petitioners prove the age and earnings of the deceased as stated in the claim petition?
3) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sri. Mahesh?
4) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.333/2021  5) What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 21 documents at Ex.P.1 to 21 and closed her side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondent No.1 and 2 did not choose to lead evidence.

6. Having heard Arguments by both side and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : In the Affirmative Issue No.4 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.5 : As per the Final Order for the following :

It is the case of the Petitioners that the husband of the Petitioner No.1 L.C. Mahesh was died in the accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Chevrolet Beat LT bearing Reg.No.25 Z1847.
8.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 had denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re iterated the averments made in the petition.
PW1 has relied on Ex.P1 to Ex.P21 and she has reiterated the Petition averments in her Chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar, Spot Sketch, Vehicle Seizer mahazar, IMV report, Police intimation and Charge sheet.

10. Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P 1 & 2 are the Certified copies of FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one S.L. Karthik S/o Srinivasa, the Hosakote Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.25Z1847 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC and u/s 187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.3 and 4 are the Spot mahazar and Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and Sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.5 is the Vehicle Seizer mahazar.
Ex.P6 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any SCCH 15 9 MVC No.333/2021 mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Ex.P7 is the Certified copy of Police intimation.

Ex.P8 is the Certified copy of the Charge Sheet which shows that the Hosakote Police has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC and U/s 187 of IMV Act.

PW1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.2.

But nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
12.

The ChargeSheet is the material document which clearly shows that the I.O. has Charge sheeted the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279, 304(A) of SCCH 15 10 MVC No.333/2021 IPC and U/s 187 of IMV Act.
The Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions.
Hence, the Respondent No.2 has failed to substantiate its Objection Statement Contentions.

Having regard to the facts and Rupa M vs The Partner Edge Solutions on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98235079/
4 circumstances of the case and oral and documentary evidence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have proved the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the husband of PW.1 was succumbed to the injuries.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "in the Affirmative."

13. Issue No.2 to 4: All these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.
14.
Though the Respondent No.2 putforth number of suggestions denying the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased Mahesh, the PW.1 has denied the said suggestions.
To SCCH 15 11 MVC No.333/2021 prove their relationship with the deceased Mahesh, the PW.1 has relied on Ex.P14 and 16 which shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.

Further, the PW.1 has produced Genealogical tree issued by the Deputy Tahasildar, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District which also shows the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased Mahesh.
Further, PW.1 has produced Ex.P11 - the Death Certificate of the Mahesh which shows the name of the father and mother as Late Chinnappa and Late Jayamma.

So,
it also crystal clear that the parents of the deceased Mahesh already expired prior to the death of Mahesh. Further, PW.1 has produced the Birth Certificates of the Petitioner No.2 and 3 i.e., Ex.P18 and 19 which also shows the name Mahesh and PW.1 as their parents.
Hence, by producing all these documents, the Petitioners have proved their relationship with the deceased Mahesh.
As the Petitioners are the L.Rs of deceased L.C. Mahesh, they entitled for the compensation.

In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 40 years and deceased was working as a Technician at Celebrations Apparel Limited and doing Agriculture and Real Estate and was earning Rs.3,00,000/ per month.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P12 - Certificate issued by the Authorised Signatory of Silver Spark Apparel Ltd., But, she has not examined the author of the said document.
PW.1 also produced RTC at Ex.P13.
But, the said property stands in the name of deceased Mahesh jointly with his brothers.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.14,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
16. Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased L.C. Mahesh as 40 years at the time of the accident.
In the PM report i.e., Ex.P.20 and Ex.P21 - Inquest mahazar the age of the deceased was shown as 45 years.
The PW.1 has not produced any other documents for age proof.

Hence, in the absence of SCCH 15 13 MVC No.333/2021 any other documents, the age mentioned in the Ex.P.20 &
21 i.e., PM report and Inquest Mahazer i.e., 45 years to be taken for consideration.
17. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:

sentences.text: The deceased has left behind his wife and children.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are children and they are considered as dependents on the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
wherein Hon'ble Apex SCCH 15 14 MVC No.333/2021 Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/
and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are children of the deceased L.C. Mahesh, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 40,000/ towards loss of consortium and Rupees 15,000/ towards loss of estate and Rupees 15,000/ towards funeral expenses.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
19.

Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and support in her young age and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased and they lost father's love and care in their young age.

Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the SCCH 15 15 MVC No.333/2021 opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
20. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
21.

It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was at Rs.14,500/ pm.
22.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi

 "Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged : 21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of Rupa M vs The Partner Edge Solutions on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98235079/
6 income of the deceased towards future prospects "

sentences.text:
Held :  yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40

entities.text: Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Upholding objections of insurance company that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent SCCH 15 17 MVC No.333/2021 made by the Tribunal for future prospects while computing compensation -
Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held:

Yes: there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork: executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding 40 per cent of income for future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that: "In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 25% when the age is between 40 to 50 years".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 45 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future SCCH 15 18 MVC No.333/2021 prospects 25% of the income has to be added.
So, 25% of Rs.14,500/ comes to Rs.3,625/.
Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.18,125/ p.m. (Rs.14,500/ + Rs.3,625/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 14.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has pleased to held that where the number of dependent of family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

23. After deducting 1/3rd towards his personal expenses in Rs.18,125/, it comes to Rs.12,084/
(Rs.18,125/  6,041/) and multiplier applied is 14 which comes to Rs.20,30,112/ (12,084 x 12 x 14).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.20,30,112/ towards loss of dependency.

TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/

3 . Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 15,000/
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/ of dead body 6.

Loss of Dependency Rs.20,30,112/ Total Rs.21,55,112/ Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.21,55,112/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

25. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending SCCH 15 20 MVC No.333/2021 Chevrolet Beat LT bearing Reg.No.25Z1847.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner, Respondent No.2 is the insurer and the Respondent No.3 is the driver of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy at the time of accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 "in the Affirmative" and Issue No.2 and 4 are "Partly in the Affirmative".
26. Issue No.5:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,55,112/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
 SCCH 15 21 MVC No.333/2021  ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the  Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.21,55,112/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned SCCH 15 22 MVC No.333/2021 among them are as shown below:

The ChargeSheet is the material document which clearly shows that the I.O. has Charge sheeted the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279, 304(A) of SCCH 15 10 MVC No.333/2021 IPC and U/s 187 of IMV Act.
The Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions.
Hence, the Respondent No.2 has failed to substantiate its Objection Statement Contentions.
Hence, by producing all these documents, the Petitioners have proved their relationship with the deceased Mahesh.
As the Petitioners are the L.Rs of deceased L.C. Mahesh, they entitled for the compensation.
In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 40 years and deceased was working as a Technician at Celebrations Apparel Limited and doing Agriculture and Real Estate and was earning Rs.3,00,000/ per month.
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 14.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner, Respondent No.2 is the insurer and the Respondent No.3 is the driver of the offending vehicle.

1. Loss of consortium Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/
3 . Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 15,000/
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/ of dead body 6.
Loss of Dependency Rs.20,30,112/ Total Rs.21,55,112/ Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.21,55,112/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 "in the Affirmative" and Issue No.2 and 4 are "Partly in the Affirmative".
26. Issue No.5:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,55,112/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
 SCCH 15 21 MVC No.333/2021  ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the  Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.21,55,112/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned SCCH 15 22 MVC No.333/2021 among them are as shown below:
Rupa M vs The Partner Edge Solutions on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98235079/
8 1) 60% to the Petitioner No.1.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of Epayment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
The entire amount awarded to the minor Petitioner No.2 and 3 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank till they attains age of majority.
Further, the natural guardian/mother of the minor SCCH 15 23 MVC No.333/2021 Petitioner No.2 and 3 is permitted to withdraw the interest on the said Fixed deposit periodically to the best interest of the minor Petitioner.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/.
 Draw Award accordingly.
